title: First meeting with Les Hite and Lionel Hampton
summary: At a Pasadena College dance Brown played with the newly arrived Les Hite and drummer Lionel Hampton and began a close friendship with both.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Oh, no, no, you just paid your dues, and you didn't get anything out of it. At this point I would like to inject one of my favorite recollections. It happened when I was over in Pasadena College. Lionel Hampton and Les Hite came west from Chicago, and one of their first stops was to play a school dance over in Pasadena.
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION

Interview with Lawrence Brown
by Patricia Willard
Reel Two

Los Angeles, California
July 1976

PROCEEDINGS
At this point I'd like to inject one of my favorite recollections. There were two fellows that came out West from Chicago. One was named Les Hite, the other was named Lionel Hampton.
And their first job in California was a little dance date at Pasadena College which I was lucky enough to play with them at. And that was my first meeting with the great Lionel Hampton.

Of course at that time he was a drummer. And his only other musical activity was the two finger playing on the piano which a lot of you remember or even have heard records of -- which he was most adept at.
Well at that time was -- just the two of them came out and hired Los Angeles musicians to play with them for their concert, or what?
Now I think there was a piano player -- we had good musicians over there too. I think Henry Prince, a very good piano player, was one of the members of the group.
There were only five of us at this dance engagement so -- it's so far back you know. That's years and years, and centuries ago. So I don't remember too much about it.
But I distinctly remember because later on, I became very close with both of these fellows.
Uh-huh. Do you remember who all played
No. Piano, drums, saxophone, and trombone. And I think that's the only instruments. I don't think there's any -- it was a small -- one of these small school dances you know. A little class things.
Well that would have been about 1921.
Around '25 or '6 -- long in there. I don't remember exactly.
Were either Les Hite or Lionel Hampton well known in this area?
No, no, they were just coming out I think on their own. I don't know why they came even. But they came out and I was one of the first that met them.
